Maintenance Report — MNT-0190-005

Asset: WELL-0190 (NE-08 Well 190, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 07 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 08 Jul 2023 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 17 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0190-0038 on 2023-07-06 Report written: 10 Jul 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0190-0038 at 10:00 on 2023-07-06 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.6% of the pad area, estimated 4.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 262 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 210 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 4.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0190-005 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.89% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0190-006

Asset: WELL-0190 (NE-08 Well 190, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 29 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 09 Aug 2023 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 272 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0190-0041 on 2023-07-27 Report written: 09 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0190-0041 showed the wellhead at 37.1 °C with the air at 32.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0190-023

Asset: WELL-0190 (NE-08 Well 190, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 13 Sep 2025 08:00 · Finished: 24 Sep 2025 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 257 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0190-0149 on 2025-09-11 Report written: 25 Sep 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0190-0149 showed the wellhead at 36.6 °C with the air at 31.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0190-023 (WS-06).
